about: Corroboration controls for the evidence lake. Built 2026-10-27 to calibrate one number: how many points reach two independent research groups. On ohsv-iv-delivery that was 0 of 30, which is uninterpretable alone - essentially one first-in-human IV oHSV trial exists, so a faithful report of that literature SHOULD find little corroboration. These two cases ask the same question shapes of densely corroborated literatures. pd1-melanoma-os pairs with tvec-os-randomised; ace2-sars2-receptor pairs with ohsv-iv-delivery. KEY PAPERS ARE GROUPED BY STUDY, NOT BY PAPER. Revised 2026-10-27 after the first run: the original version keyed on the 2015 primary trial reports, and the lake correctly cited the mature follow-up analyses instead (KEYNOTE-006 5-year, CheckMate 067 at 6.5 years) - which are the better sources for an overall-survival question. Scoring the report 0/3 for that would have measured the case file, not the pipeline. Each clinical trial and each structural approach is now a role=alternative group, satisfied by any of its reports. Note lakemap.py reads role/group; eval.py still flat-counts key_papers, so its key_cited/key_total is a weaker signal here - read lakemap's requirement score. Identifiers confirmed against Europe PMC 2026-10-27; a title-only search returns letters, commentaries, addenda and errata carrying the original's title, so every entry carries a DOI.

cases.question: What overall survival benefit have PD-1 inhibitors demonstrated in randomised trials in advanced melanoma?

key_papers.label: KEYNOTE-006 primary (Robert 2015 NEJM; pembrolizumab vs ipilimumab)
key_papers.title: pembrolizumab versus ipilimumab in advanced melanoma

key_papers.label: KEYNOTE-006 final OS (Schachter 2017 Lancet)
key_papers.title: pembrolizumab versus ipilimumab for advanced melanoma: final overall survival results

key_papers.label: KEYNOTE-006 5-year post-hoc (Robert 2019 Lancet Oncol)
key_papers.title: pembrolizumab versus ipilimumab in advanced melanoma (keynote-006): post-hoc 5-year results

key_papers.label: CheckMate 067 primary (Larkin 2015 NEJM; three-arm)
key_papers.title: combined nivolumab and ipilimumab or monotherapy in untreated melanoma

key_papers.label: CheckMate 067 OS (Wolchok 2017 NEJM)
key_papers.title: overall survival with combined nivolumab and ipilimumab in advanced melanoma

key_papers.label: CheckMate 067 long-term (Wolchok 2022 JCO; 6.5-year)
key_papers.title: long-term outcomes with nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab alone versus ipilimumab

key_papers.label: CheckMate 066 (Robert 2015 NEJM; nivolumab vs dacarbazine - the only PD-1 vs chemotherapy RCT here)
key_papers.title: nivolumab in previously untreated melanoma without braf mutation

cases.notes: The positive-control twin of tvec-os-randomised: same disease, same endpoint, same trial design, but several independent randomised phase III trials report a significant overall survival benefit rather than one trial reporting a descriptive secondary endpoint. A correct answer must state that PD-1 blockade improved OS against the active comparator in more than one randomised trial, and must keep the comparators straight - pembrolizumab was tested against ipilimumab, nivolumab against dacarbazine in BRAF-wild-type disease, and CheckMate 067 compared the combination and each monotherapy. None of the NEJM trial reports is open access, so all three will be read as abstracts; RCT abstracts carry the hazard ratios, which makes this case a test of the abstract-only path as well. Watch the group rule: the same investigators appear across these trials (Robert is an author on both KEYNOTE-006 and CheckMate 066), so author-overlap may collapse genuinely separate trials into one group. That is a property of melanoma trial authorship and a fair test of the same_group rule, not a defect in the case. Revised 2026-10-27: key papers are grouped per trial, since any report of a trial establishes that trial's OS result and the mature follow-ups are the better sources for this question. The first run cited three CheckMate 067 reports and two KEYNOTE-006 reports while naming neither trial for its most prominent reference, so a reader counts one trial as three - which is also why the corroboration number needs the study grouping before it means anything. CheckMate 066 was genuinely absent from the first run: no PD-1-versus-chemotherapy evidence appeared at all, and no gap line said so.

expect.note: eval.py does not read this block; it records the prediction so the result is a two-sided test rather than a number without a range. Corroboration counts come from truthinator run over the finished lake.
expect.rationale: At least three randomised phase III trials report OS for this drug class in this disease. A report finding no corroboration here indicates a pipeline limit, not a thin literature.

scoring.must_surface: KEYNOTE-006 (pembrolizumab versus ipilimumab) and at least one of CheckMate 066 / CheckMate 067. The answer must name overall survival as a met endpoint in at least two independent randomised trials, and must name the comparator in each - ipilimumab for KEYNOTE-006, dacarbazine for CheckMate 066, ipilimumab and nivolumab monotherapy for CheckMate 067.
scoring.must_not_flatten: Fail any answer that (a) reports response rate or progression-free survival in place of overall survival; (b) describes the comparator as placebo or best supportive care in any of these trials; (c) presents CheckMate 067 as having demonstrated superior overall survival for the combination over nivolumab alone, which it was not powered to test; (d) pools pembrolizumab and nivolumab results into a single trial result; (e) cites later follow-up analyses as if they were the primary randomised comparison.
